observations.trace: from_presented_scene checks centered origins, positive finite spacing, dimensions, height cardinality and strictly expanding calculated half extents. It delegates rectangle clipping, playable-boundary splitting and height interpolation to the inspected vista_surface functions. Those helpers retain optional no-coarser and no-playable-terrain modes; final typed point/elevation admissions can reject nonfinite outputs. Very large finite spacing can overflow a calculated extent, but a full valid producer-to-outcome witness is not established.

observations.trace: measure_region reports required and accumulated covered area together with its maximum grade, and does not claim a slope certifies collision or complete coverage. The compare-city-terrain example exposes separate grade-bound and coverage-complete booleans, and a separate complete surface comparison; the grade flag alone is not evidence that the example asserts full coverage. GeographicGrade is an observed nonnegative finite f64 quantity, distinct from configured SupportGrade.

observations.trace: SupportViolation::maximum converts finite nonnegative Count controls from f64 to u64 without an explicit fractional or overflow check. Inspected membership, binding, reservation, source-sample and enclosure count cases use finite literal failure controls, while vertex_start replaces the adapter result with direct checked integer counts or structured Unmeasurable. Minimum-bound Unmeasurable numerical port returns zero discrepancy by static reasoning, while its structured enum retains unit and bound. Repository text search found discrepancy_value calls only in test source at this revision; attempted_metres also reaches the diagnostic example to sort nearby streets.

conditional_findings.first_contract: A maximum physical grade operation should report its admitted finite non-flat support mesh accurately or explicitly identify an unmeasurable calculation.
conditional_findings.trace: The original059 source-level example uses a=(0,0,0), b=(1e20,1e20,0), c=(0,1e20,1e20), nonzero property/member, positive finite tolerance and three distinct in-range indices. Standalone SupportMeshWire validates these fields but does not check the cross product. In ordinary f32 arithmetic its normal products overflow and the horizontal-to-vertical ratio becomes infinity/infinity NaN; f32::max with initial zero ignores that NaN, so maximum_grade returns zero by static source reasoning. The true planar grade is sqrt(2). Pinned glam source shows the cross and Vec2 length operations; the locally installed channel-matching rust-src describes f32::max semantics. No input was decoded and no product/native operation was run.
conditional_findings.safeguards_and_limits: This is a current reassessment of original059 Adler Lens11 finding and Segovb Lens12 connected review, not a new historical finding or checkpoint3821 restoration. The current PropertySupportSurface::validate_encoded checks normal finiteness and nonzero vertical component before maximum_grade, so rejects this particular 1e20 example in final generated or decoded surface admission. The earlier selected-terrain inference was explicitly withdrawn and remains withdrawn. Entry mesh construction and example report call maximum_grade, but no shown normal producer reaches this exact standalone wire example. The installed rust-src is locally identified by the repository channel, not independently verified upstream artifact bytes. Other finite-normal precision cases, the complete generated path, native Avian collider and exact aliases remain open.

Trace all actual generated mesh, street entry and report consumers; compare finite precision of complete measurement with configured grade without imposing arbitrary gameplay height bounds.
If repair warranted, accurately represent or reject invalid/unmeasurable grade, preserve ordinary sloped surfaces and native collision ownership; later validate only when authorized.
Keep prior final-validator qualification, same-lens reuse and prospective role2695 unread ranges intact; deduplicate only by demonstrated first contract.
